- 🍽️ Restaurants, cafés and services within the complex
- 📸 Excellent views of the Tenerife Auditorium and the Atlantic

### Recommendation
Combine the visit with a walk to the Tenerife Auditorium, the Palmetum or the historic centre of Santa Cruz. One of the best options for enjoying the sea and sun in the island capital, especially if you want comfort and all services in one place.

pois.name: Lago Martiánez
pois.shortDescription: César Manrique's masterpiece in Puerto de la Cruz: saltwater lagoons and volcanic art
pois.description:
The **Costa Martiánez Tourist Complex**, popularly known as **Lago Martiánez**, is one of the most emblematic spaces on Tenerife and one of César Manrique's most important works. Opened in 1977 facing the Atlantic Ocean, this spectacular complex combines saltwater pools, gardens, sculptures and architecture integrated into the volcanic landscape of the Canary Islands.

### The visit
The complex covers more than 100,000 square metres and is formed by a large central artificial lagoon surrounded by several pools, islets, waterfalls and landscaped areas. The black volcanic stone, subtropical vegetation and sculptures designed by César Manrique create a unique environment where art and nature coexist in perfect harmony.

Located in the heart of Puerto de la Cruz, it offers impressive views of the Atlantic Ocean and the north Tenerife coast. In addition to the bathing areas, the complex has restaurants, terraces and spacious areas to relax in the sun.

The work is considered one of the finest examples of landscape architecture in the Canary Islands and one of the most recognised projects of César Manrique's artistic legacy outside Lanzarote.

### Before you go
- 🎨 Designed by César Manrique, one of the most influential figures in Canarian art
- 🌊 Multiple pools and a large saltwater lagoon
- 🌴 Wide landscaped areas and sunbathing spaces
- 📸 One of the most photogenic places in Puerto de la Cruz
- 🍽️ Restaurants and services within the complex
- 🚶 Just a few minutes from the historic centre of the town

### Recommendation
Dedicate at least half a day to enjoy the complex and combine it with a visit to the Paseo de San Telmo, Plaza del Charco or Playa Jardín. Lago Martiánez is much more than a bathing area: it is one of the most important open-air artworks in the Canary Islands and an unmissable visit in Puerto de la Cruz.

municipios.name: Santa Cruz de Tenerife
municipios.shortDescription: Capital of Tenerife, home to Spain's most famous Carnival
municipios.description: Santa Cruz de Tenerife is the island's capital and one of the most vibrant cities in the Canary Islands. The Santa Cruz Carnival, declared an International Tourist Interest event, is the second largest in the world after Rio. Calatrava's Auditorium and García Sanabria Park give the city a singular cultural profile. The port is one of the most active in the Atlantic.

municipios.name: La Orotava
municipios.shortDescription: Teide National Park, Spain's highest volcano and UNESCO World Heritage Site
municipios.description: La Orotava is home to the heart of Teide National Park, the most visited volcano in the world and Spain's highest peak at 3,715 metres. The lunar solidified lava landscapes, the sea of clouds surrounding the caldera and the cable car to the summit make this municipality the essential visit in Tenerife. UNESCO World Heritage Site.

municipios.name: Santiago del Teide
municipios.shortDescription: Los Gigantes cliffs and whale watching on the west coast of Tenerife
municipios.description: Santiago del Teide is the municipality of Tenerife's spectacular west coast. Los Gigantes, cliffs up to 600 metres tall dropping vertically into the Atlantic, create the most dramatic landscape on the island. The waters offshore are home to one of the most stable cetacean colonies in Europe: dolphins and pilot whales can be spotted almost daily in season.

municipios.name: Arona
municipios.shortDescription: Los Cristianos and the southern beaches: Tenerife's tourist heartland
municipios.description: Arona is home to some of the most popular beaches in southern Tenerife, with Los Cristianos as the centrepiece. A fishing harbour transformed into a tourist destination, it retains the authenticity of its historic streets alongside top-quality restaurants, entertainment and water sports. This is also where the ferries to La Gomera and El Hierro depart.

municipios.name: Adeje
municipios.shortDescription: Costa Adeje and Playa del Duque: the most exclusive and elegant area in southern Tenerife
municipios.description: Adeje is the municipality of Costa Adeje, the premium tourist area in southern Tenerife. Playa del Duque, surrounded by the island's most luxurious hotels, and the neighbouring Playa de Fañabé are its coastal highlights. The Barranco del Infierno, accessible from the historic town centre, offers a spectacular hiking route between sheer vertical walls.

municipios.name: Granadilla de Abona
municipios.shortDescription: El Médano and Spain's best windsurfing and kitesurfing, 5 minutes from the airport
municipios.description: Granadilla de Abona is home to El Médano, Spain's most famous windsurfing and kitesurfing spot. Its long fine-sand beaches and constant trade winds attract water sports enthusiasts from all over the world, while the Roque del Moro is one of the south's most iconic natural landmarks. The international Reina Sofía Airport (TFS) is just 5 minutes away by car.

municipios.name: San Cristóbal de La Laguna
municipios.shortDescription: UNESCO World Heritage City and gateway to the Anaga Rural Park
municipios.description: La Laguna is Tenerife's university city and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, with a colonial historic centre that influenced the design of Latin American cities. It is also the gateway to the Anaga Rural Park, home to the largest laurel forest in Europe, where natural gems such as Playa de Benijo and the Roques de Anaga await.

municipios.name: Puerto de la Cruz
municipios.shortDescription: The north's tourist capital: Martiánez pools, Loro Parque and Tenerife's original historic resort
municipios.description: Puerto de la Cruz is Tenerife's historic tourist destination and the most important in the north of the island. The Lago Martiánez pools designed by César Manrique, the Botanical Garden — one of Spain's oldest — and Loro Parque make this municipality the cultural and leisure reference of the north. Its historic centre retains the charm of a town that received European aristocracy for decades.

municipios.name: Güímar
municipios.shortDescription: The mysterious stepped pyramids in the quiet southeast of Tenerife
municipios.description: Güímar is a municipality in the southeast of Tenerife famous for its stepped pyramids of black volcanic stone, studied by Thor Heyerdahl in the 1990s. The surrounding area is one of the quietest and most authentic on the island, far from the mass tourism of the south.

municipios.name: Vilaflor
municipios.shortDescription: Spain's highest village: Canarian pine forest, Paisaje Lunar and gateway to the National Park
municipios.description: Vilaflor, at 1,400 metres altitude, is Spain's highest village and the southern gateway to Teide National Park. Its ancient Canarian pine forests are home to Paisaje Lunar, one of the most singular geological formations in the Canary Islands.
